newsitem.title: UK: LME metals end shaky, more losses expected.
newsitem.headline: LME metals end shaky, more losses expected.

text.p: LME base metals finished wobbly on Thursday afternoon after aluminium carved out a fresh 2-1/4 year low and copper failed to hold above the $1,900 level.
"The close on copper certainly is not very encouraging," one trader said.
Three months aluminium dived to a fresh 2-1/4 year low of $1,340 in the morning but clawed its way up to close at $1,352, a $25 loss, on trade buying, mostly from the Far East.
"I'm not convinced it's enough to keep it up," a trader said. Next major support was pegged around $1,330, the lows of early June 1994, then the psychological $1,300 region.
Resistance was expected at $1,357, the morning's break out area.
But chartist William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff regarded the market as bottoming-out, noting that technical indicators have turned up and the market was oversold.
"I would look for a bounce in the next couple of days, or at least consolidation at these levels," he said.
In copper, prices failed to stray too far from either side of the $1,900 level after an early slide. It successively popped above the $1,900 parapet, but each time ducked back below.
But the market expected stocks to continue their recent declines on Friday after a draw of 7,825 tonnes on Tuesday.
The cash/threes spread came in, indicated level after trading as high as a $5 contango in the morning and compared to a $3 contango on Wednesday afternoon.
Adams thought the market may see some short-term strength, but producers would see it as a selling opportunity.

Nickel rechallenged the upside in the afternoon but it was capped by selling around $7,100 and $7,120. The market ended at $7,100, up $5, after getting a modest boost from news that WMC Ltd shut a mine in Western Australia after a miner was killed.
Last business in tin was $20 weaker at $6,040 after it held to a tight range.
Lead finished slightly higher at $764, up $4, with a nice base built around the $750 level, Adams said.
"We've seen a lot of liquidation recently but I think the loose longs are now out of the market," he added.
Zinc closed the day a touch weaker at $1,018.50, down $2.50 and alloy was marked down with the primary market to end at $1,208/10 versus $1,225.
